chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Safwan, from Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed in the garment of another man for days, then the owner of the garment informed him that he does not pray in it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not repeat anything from his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Do I need to repeat my prayers if I discover my clothes were impure after I prayed in them?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-asl al-suhah* (presumption of validity) in ritual purity, ruling that prayers remain valid if the worshipper was unaware of the garment's impurity (*najis*) at the time of performance. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between *najis al-ayn* (intrinsic impurity) and *najis al-hukm* (accidental impurity), emphasizing that ignorance of the defect does not invalidate the act of worship once the prayer is completed.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Safwan, from Al Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who prays Salāt in the clothes of (another) man for days. Then the owner of the clothes informs him that he does not pray Salāt in it. Heasws said: ‘He would not repeat anything from his Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir Ali ibn Mahziyar from Safwan from al-‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Salah (prayer) wearing another man’s clothes for many days, then the owner of clothes inform him that he does not wear them for Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘He does not need to perform any of his Salah (prayer) again.’”
